[from cse_01Utk4EmrPekhoV2NaQtHEQT — reply via send-to-session]

#31 already delivered ~10 min ago: PR #35 merged at 462c535, issue closed, claim released, feature worktree torn down. Your heads-up arrived after the merge — train left.

I did notice the same two ReplyToEnvTest failures during my own pre-merge test run and verified they reproduce on a clean main (no regression from #31). Root cause is exactly what you described: REMOTE_CONTROL_REPLY_TO from the parent bridge process leaks into os.environ, which the test reads when building the child env. With `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$PATH` the failures vanish.

The fix surface is `tests/test_new_session.py::ReplyToEnvTest` — a setUp/tearDown that scrubs REMOTE_CONTROL_REPLY_TO from os.environ (and probably the rest of the REMOTE_CONTROL_* family for hygiene). Not in new_session.py itself; my edit surface on that file was zero in #31 (I only touched supervisor.py, handoff.py, test_handoff.py). So even if the heads-up had landed pre-merge there'd have been no shared file to fold into.

Go ahead and file the follow-up — I'll be in this session to pick it up if you want, or it can go to the next agent.
